mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and profits are squeezed.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment, measured by the UNRATE series, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will weigh on corporate earnings and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (UMCSENT) rises concurrently with UNRATE, indicating a 'soft landing' scenario where earnings hold up despite labor market weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise faster than the rate of GDP growth, it signals overinvestment in the housing sector that will lead to an economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST y/y growth > GDPC1 y/y growth
failure_condition: Housing starts growth reverts back below GDP growth within 3 months, indicating the overinvestment was temporary and will not lead to a sustained slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the CPI inflation gauge, not accompanied by a corresponding rise in the federal funds rate, signals a loss of credibility for the Fed's inflation-fighting resolve and will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as real yields are compressed.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: The Fed delivers an emergency inter-meeting rate hike within 2 weeks of the trigger, restoring credibility and stabilizing real yields.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth decelerates sharply, indicating a rapidly weakening labor market, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as companies scramble to adjust earnings expectations lower.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims (ICSA) begin falling immediately after the PAYEMS slowdown, indicating the labor market weakness was temporary and will not lead to sustained earnings downgrades.

mechanism_narrative: Real estate investment (RSAFS) rising as a share of GDP points to a speculative bubble in the housing market that will eventually burst, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the bubble unwinds.
failure_condition: The share of RSAFS in GDP mean-reverts back below 0.18 within 6 months, indicating the bubble was smaller than feared and will not lead to a major unwind.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the CPI inflation gauge is falling, it signals a successful disinflationary tightening cycle by the Fed that will lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as real yields stabilize at a lower level.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL falling over 3 months
failure_condition: The Fed abruptly pauses or reverses its tightening cycle, indicating that the disinflation was not achieved sustainably and real yields will remain elevated.
